newsitem.title: UK: European gas oil cargoes revive, barges stalled.
newsitem.headline: European gas oil cargoes revive, barges stalled.

text.p: Tepid demand stirred activity and supported premiums in an otherwise quiet NWE gas oil cargo market on Friday, but barge activity was limp with premiums barely steady in inactive volumes, traders said.
Jan IPE benchmark futures ended $8.50 higher at $213.75 a tonne on on the back of NYMEX gains built on forecasts of cold European and U.S. weather.

Flat German inland demand kept barges in the doldrums with most wholesalers covered until year end and reluctant to tackle stubborn backwardation. A barge of refinery grade heating oil was done at Jan IPE flat fob ARA for second half Dec.
That early deal was around 75 cents firmer. Later buying interest was Jan IPE -$1 with sellers around flat.

Cargoes saw more action. French grade low sulphur diesel (-5/-15) was done at Jan IPE +$14, around unchanged, and was offered at Jan IPE +$13 and bid at +$12. A bidder also emerged at +$15 but retreated after attracting an offer of +$15.50.

On cargoes, 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil traded at Jan IPE +$4.50, unchanged. Distressed Russian cargoes were still seen slightly above the screen. -- William Maclean London newsroom +44 171 542 7646
